title: Feature flag staged rollouts for Dedicated: per-tenant allowlist + operator override
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
description: Context: Dedicated staged rollouts are landing behind the existing rollout primitives, but we do NOT want this to be generally available to all Dedicated tenants on day 1. We need an explicit allowlist (per tenant) and an internal operator override for incident response / dogfood so we can unblock SRE + CS during beta without broad exposure. This PR adds feature flag gating to ensure staged rollouts are enabled for Dedicated pools only when (a) the tenant is allowlisted, OR (b) an internal operator is acting with an explicit override (audited). Summary of changes: Adds a new control-plane feature gate `dedicated.staged_rollouts` evaluated at request time for staged rollout plan CRUD + status endpoints and for routing policy evaluation when a pool references a staged rollout plan; Implements a per-tenant allowlist store (backed by Control Plane config DB) with cached reads and a safe default of deny; Adds an internal-only operator override path (requires operator role + `rollout.override` permission) using an explicit request header `X-Redwood-Operator-Override: dedicated-staged-rollouts` (Console/admin tools only); Emits audit events for allowlist changes and for each operator override usage (includes actor, tenant_id, pool_id when available, reason string, request_id); Exposes a minimal admin endpoint for updating the allowlist (internal network + RBAC) and a CLI helper used by SRE during beta enablement; Updates docs/comments in the rollout endpoints to clarify expected failure mode: when disabled, the API returns 403 with `feature_not_enabled` and routing falls back to existing pool-level rollout behavior (no staged weights). Behavior details: Customer-facing Dedicated tenants (non-allowlisted) will not see staged rollout UI/actions even if they can access Dedicated pools; Console backend should treat 403(feature_not_enabled) as 'staged rollouts not available' and show the existing pool update flow; Operator override is intended for Redwood internal dogfood and incident mitigation only; it does not persist any allowlist state and is expected to be used with a ticket/incident reference in the `reason` field; The flag does NOT apply to Hosted (API) rollouts; this is strictly for Dedicated pools / tenant scope. Security & compliance notes: Allowlist updates and operator override usage are both audit logged and included in the existing audit export pipeline (SOC2 change management mapping for SUP-3981); Operator override requires both an internal identity and explicit permission; we intentionally require an explicit header so it cannot be triggered accidentally by a normal Console request path. Testing: Unit tests for gate evaluation and RBAC conditions; Integration tests for: non-allowlisted tenant gets 403; allowlisted tenant can create/update staged rollout plan; operator override can proceed for non-allowlisted tenant; routing policy evaluation blocks staged plan reference when disabled; Added a canary test that ensures the default is deny for new tenants. Rollout plan: Land behind `feature_gate.dedicated.staged_rollouts` default OFF; SRE will enable allowlist for dogfood pools, then 2 beta customers (ENG-5134); No customer-visible docs changes in this PR (those are in redwood-docs PR #1442). Notes/links: Epic PM-418; CS references: SUP-3924 (traffic split confusion), SUP-3981 (audit trail request).
commits: control-plane: add FeatureGate key dedicated.staged_rollouts and evaluation helper
control-plane: implement tenant allowlist store + caching
api: gate staged rollout plan endpoints behind allowlist/override
routing: block staged rollout plan reference when feature gate disabled; fall back to legacy behavior
security: add audit events for allowlist updates and operator override usage
cli/admin: add allowlist management command for SRE beta enablement
tests: add unit + integration tests for gating behavior
review_conversation: Marcus Lin: The operator override needs to be explicitly auditable. Can we ensure the reason is required and captured in audit logs? Also, please confirm override can't be used by enterprise tenant admins.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Added `reason` as required for override path (400 if missing) and included it in the audit event payload. Override is gated by internal operator auth + `rollout.override` permission; enterprise admins won't have that permission and the endpoint is internal-only.
Sean Gallagher: Default-deny is good. What happens if the allowlist store is unavailable or cache is stale? Prefer fail-closed for safety.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Implemented fail-closed: if allowlist read fails, gate returns disabled and endpoints return 503 for internal admin calls, 403(feature_not_enabled) for customer calls. Cache TTL is 60s; admin updates invalidate cache immediately via pubsub event.
Mina Haddad: Routing fallback behavior needs to be deterministic. If staged plan reference is blocked, do we error or ignore?

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): We ignore staged plan reference when disabled and proceed with legacy pool-level behavior, with a structured warning log + metric increment. This avoids turning a config mismatch into an outage.
Ethan Park: Please add a quick integration test that a non-allowlisted tenant cannot even list rollout plans (not just create).
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Added coverage in `dedicated_rollouts_feature_gate.test.ts` for list/get/status (403) and verified console backend handles it.
Lauren Bishop: This is aligned with beta plan. Make sure the allowlist key is tenant-scoped (not pool-scoped) so we can onboard multiple pools per customer without repeating ops steps.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Confirmed: allowlist is tenant-scoped; operator override can optionally include pool_id for audit context but isn't required.
release_notes: Internal: Dedicated staged rollouts can now be enabled per-tenant via allowlist; internal operators may use an audited override for dogfood/incident response. No general customer availability change (default off).
